headline: Montgomery sees Magellan Financial Group (MFG) as a 'mini Macquarie' ground-floor opportunity following ACCC approval of Barrenjoey acquisition
reasoning: Montgomery argues the ACCC-approved merger with Barrenjoey fundamentally transforms Magellan from a standalone funds manager plagued by outflows into a diversified financial services group. The combined entity will have a ~$2 billion balance sheet including ~$694 million in net cash, providing a war chest for future investments. The deal is expected to be earnings dilutive near-term but strongly accretive by FY2028 as operating leverage and cross-selling opportunities materialise. Barrenjoey's advisory, capital markets, equities and fixed income operations are expected to drive double-digit earnings growth, while Magellan's global distribution networks could supercharge Barrenjoey's Private Capital arm. Leadership of the combined group — renamed Barrenjoey Group Limited (BJY) — will be led by some of the most connected people in Australian finance, including Brian Benari as Group CEO and David Gonski as Group Chairman. The comparison to Macquarie Bank's 1,400% capital gain since 1999 frames the long-term compounding potential of the thesis.
quote: The opportunity to buy a mini Macquarie on the ground floor might be Magellan Financial Group (ASX: MFG). On 11 June 2026, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) decided to approve Magellan Financial Group Ltd's (MFG) proposed acquisition of the remaining shares in Barrenjoey Capital Partners Group Holdings Pty Limited (Barrenjoey) that it does not already own, in return for equity in MFG (the Acquisition). The bullish view is the merger fundamentally shifts Magellan from a standalone funds manager – which has been plagued by steady outflows – into a diversified financial services operator, and one run by some of the sharpest and best-connected people in the country. By internalising Barrenjoey's high-growth, market-facing operations (advisory, capital markets, equities, and fixed income), the combined group is expected to leverage investment banking to drive double-digit earnings growth.

headline: Bear case acknowledged: Barrenjoey merger does not resolve Magellan's persistent fund outflows and introduces cyclical investment banking earnings risk
reasoning: Sceptical analysts including Morningstar and JPMorgan note that acquiring an investment bank does not fix Magellan's core problem of persistent net outflows and fee margin compression, which will still represent approximately 40% of group revenue post-merger. Investment banking is notoriously cyclical, and Barrenjoey's strong first five years occurred largely during a bull market, meaning future earnings will fluctuate with corporate deal activity. There is also a significant cultural and operational integration risk, as merging an entrepreneurial investment bank with a traditional funds manager has historically destroyed value. The speaker suspects this is effectively a reverse takeover where Barrenjoey's culture and strategy will dominate, which investors should factor into their assessment.
quote: Analysts such as Morningstar and JPMorgan, hold a more cautious outlook, at least in the near term. They highlight significant structural risks, including the fact that buying an investment bank doesn't fix Magellan's persistent net outflows and fee margin compression, which is dragging down its core funds management business, that will still account for approximately 40 per cent of group revenue after the merger. Meanwhile, it's worth keeping in mind investment banking is notoriously cyclical. While Barrenjoey has enjoyed massive growth in its first five years – much of it during a bull market – its future earnings will rise and fall with corporate deal-making and market cycles. The least optimistic analysts say investment banking introduces heavy volatility to Magellan's earnings rather than stabilising the group's income stream. Finally, the bears suggest that integrating an entrepreneurial, fast-moving investment bank with a traditional funds management firm presents a massive cultural and operational hurdle.

headline: Sandon Capital sees Magellan Financial Group turning a corner as legacy issues resolved and capital management expected in 1H 2024

MFG also resolved its long-running liability related to options over closed class units in Magellan Global Fund (MGF), agreeing to purchase up to 750 million MGF options at 10 cents each. This coincided with the responsible entity (RE) of MGF deciding to proceed with a conversion of the closed class units to open class units, thus permanently addressing the discount to net asset value (NAV) that MGF has persistently traded at. Whilst the resolution of MGF and its options will cost more than we expected, it will also bring an end to a saga that has tarnished the MFG brand for a number of years now. MFG Executive Chairman, Andrew Formica, has moved expeditiously to address a number of legacy issues. With these now largely in the rear-view mirror, we look forward to him turning his attention towards capital management in the first half of 2024.

headline: Sandon Capital launches activist campaign in Magellan Financial Group, viewing it as deeply undervalued with significant downside protection from cash and non-core assets.
reasoning: Sandon Capital launched an activist campaign in MFG during June 2023, citing deep undervaluation and market misunderstanding. The firm believes a large portion of MFG's market capitalisation is accounted for by cash and non-core investments, providing considerable downside protection. Investment underperformance post-COVID and personnel changes led to fund outflows and negative market perceptions, which Sandon views as an opportunity. Sandon has made five recommendations to the MFG Board: return excess capital to shareholders, prioritise the existing business, review the cost base, provide Share Purchase Plan relief, and accelerate Board renewal with improved diversity. Should the Board adopt these recommendations, Sandon expects a significant improvement in MFG's market price and intrinsic value.
quote: During the month, we launched our latest campaign - MFG. MFG is an Australian-based global funds management company that manages funds across three categories: Global Equities, Infrastructure Equities and Australian Equities. The company was established in 2006 and became a leading asset management franchise in Australia, especially among retail investors and independent financial advisers. However, investment underperformance as financial markets emerged from COVID-19 and then personnel change led to a loss of confidence and substantial fund outflows. Today, market perceptions of MFG are negative, and we believe the company to be deeply undervalued and misunderstood. A large portion of MFG's current market capitalisation is accounted for by cash and investments that we consider non-core. We believe this provides considerable downside protection for our investment. In order to stabilise the business, and return to strong long-term profitability, we have made five recommendations to the MFG Board. These include (1) Return excess capital to shareholders (2) Prioritise the existing business (3) Review the cost base (4) Provide further Share Purchase Plan (SPP) relief, and (5) Accelerate Board renewal and improve Board diversity. Should the MFG Board adopt our recommendations, we expect the market price and value of MFG shares to improve significantly.
